I can take a nap.\" So he slept under a tree. The Tortoise walked slowly but he never stopped. He kept moving. When the Hare woke up, the Tortoise was near the finish line. The boy cried for help. That was the third time. But the villagers did not come. They thought it was a lie. The wolf ate all the sheep. cards.back: {"full_text": "It was New Year's Eve. A little girl was walking in the street. She was barefoot and cold. She was carrying a box of matches. She was trying to sell them, but nobody bought any. She was so cold that she sat down in a corner. She lit one match to warm herself. In the light, she saw a warm stove. But the match went out. She lit another match. This time she saw a table with delicious food. She was so hungry that she wanted to eat. But the match went out again. She lit a third match. She saw a beautiful Christmas tree. \"I wish I could stay here forever,\" she said. Then she saw her grandmother, who was smiling. \"Grandma!\" she cried. \"Take me with you!\" She lit all the matches together. The grandmother took her in her arms. The next morning, people found the little girl. She had died from the cold, but she was smiling.", "translation": "这是除夕夜。一个小女孩在街上走着。她光着脚，很冷。她拿着一盒火柴，想卖掉它们，但没有人买。她太冷了，于是蹲在一个角落里。她划燃一根火柴取暖。火光中，她看到一个温暖的火炉。但火柴熄灭了。她划燃另一根火柴，这次看到一张摆满美食的桌子。她太饿了，想吃东西。但火柴又熄灭了。她划燃第三根火柴，看到一棵美丽的圣诞树。她说：“我希望我能永远待在这里。”然后她看到了微笑的祖母。“奶奶！”她喊道，“带我走吧！”她划燃了所有火柴。祖母把她抱在怀里。第二天早上，人们发现了小女孩。她冻死了，但脸上带着微笑。", "key_sentence_patterns": [{"pattern": "She was so cold that she sat down.", "explanation": "so...that... 结构表示“如此……以至于……”，用于强调程度导致结果。"}, {"pattern": "I wish I could stay here forever.", "explanation": "wish + 过去式表示对现在不可能实现的愿望。"}, {"pattern": "She was carrying a box of matches.", "explanation": "过去进行时表示在过去某个时刻正在进行的动作。"}], "key_grammar": [{"point": "过去进行时", "example": "She was walking in the street."}, {"point": "so...that...", "example": "She was so hungry that she wanted to eat."}, {"point": "wish + 过去式", "example": "I wish I could stay here."}], "vocabulary_focus": ["match", "barefoot", "corner", "warm", "stove", "delicious", "Christmas tree", "grandmother", "cry", "smiling", "died", "eve"], "common_mistakes": "常见错误：过去进行时中忘记用was/were，例如 'She walking' 应改为 'She was walking'。另外 wish后常误用现在时，如 'I wish I can stay' 应改为 'I wish I could stay'。", "tags": ["fairy tale", "Andersen", "compassion", "poverty", "Christmas"], "author": "Andersen"}

{"full_text": "A: Hello. May I speak to Mrs. Chen, please?
B: I'm sorry, she's not in right now. Can I take a message?
A: Yes, please. This is Tom from the office. Could you ask her to call me back?
B: Sure. Does she have your number?
A: Yes, she does. Thank you.
B: No problem. I'll give her the message.
A: Great. I'll call back later if she doesn't call. Goodbye.
B: Goodbye.", "translation": "A: 你好。请问我可以和陈太太通话吗？
B: 抱歉，她现在不在。需要我捎个口信吗？
A: 好的，麻烦了。我是办公室的汤姆。你能让她给我回电话吗？
B: 当然。她有你的号码吗？
A: 有的。谢谢。
B: 不客气。我会把口信转告给她。
A: 太好了。如果她没有打电话，我之后再打过来。再见。
B: 再见。", "key_sentence_patterns": [{"pattern": "May I speak to ... , please?", "explanation": "礼貌地询问是否可以与某人通话。"}, {"pattern": "Can I take a message?", "explanation": "询问是否需要帮忙传话。"}, {"pattern": "Could you ask her to ...?", "explanation": "礼貌地请求他人做某事。"}, {"pattern": "I'll call back later.", "explanation": "表示稍后再打过来。"}], "key_grammar": [{"point": "Modal verbs for polite requests (May I, Can I, Could you)", "example": "May I speak to Mrs. Chen? / Can I take a message? / Could you ask her to call me back?"}, {"point": "Present simple for states ('She's not in', 'She does')", "example": "She's not in right now. / Does she have your number?"}, {"point": "Future with 'will' for intentions ('I'll give', 'I'll call')", "example": "I'll give her the message. / I'll call back later."}, {"point": "Yes/No questions with auxiliary verbs", "example": "Does she have your number?"}, {"point": "Imperative in polite requests (Ask her to...)", "example": "Could you ask her to call me back?"}], "vocabulary_focus": ["may I", "speak to", "please", "sorry", "not in", "right now", "message", "call back", "office", "number", "later", "goodbye"], "common_mistakes": "Students often say 'I want to speak to...' instead of 'May I speak to...' which is too direct. {"full_text": "Dear Grandma,

How are you? I hope you are well. I have just finished my school exams. I am happy because I did well. I have also started a new hobby – painting. I love it! But I miss you very much. I want to visit you next month, but I need to ask Mom first. She says maybe we can come in the summer. I have not seen you for a long time. I think about you every day.

Please write back soon. Tell me about your garden. I hope the flowers are beautiful.

Love,
Tom", "translation": "亲爱的奶奶：

您好吗？希望您一切安好。我刚考完学校考试，考得不错，所以很开心。我还开始了新爱好——绘画。我很喜欢！但是我很想念您。我想下个月去看您，但得先问妈妈。她说也许我们夏天能来。我很久没见到您了。我每天都想着您。

请尽快回信。告诉我您的花园怎么样了。希望花儿很美。

爱您的，
汤姆", "key_sentence_patterns": [{"pattern": "I have just + 过去分词", "explanation": "表示刚做完某事，用于现在完成时。"}, {"pattern": "I want to + verb, but + 句子", "explanation": "表达想做什么但受到限制。"}, {"pattern": "I have not + 过去分词 + for a long time", "explanation": "表示很久没做某事了。"}], "key_grammar": [{"point": "现在完成时（简单用法）", "example": "I have just finished my school exams. / I have not seen you for a long time."}, {"point": "连词 and / but / or", "example": "I am happy because I did well. (and 隐含在并列中) / I want to visit you, but I need to ask Mom first. / Tell me about your garden. I hope the flowers are beautiful. (or 未直接出现，但可用于否定句：I don't know if I can come or not.)"}, {"point": "信函格式：称呼、正文、结束语", "example": "Dear Grandma, ... Love, Tom"}, {"point": "一般现在时和现在完成时混合", "example": "How are you? I have just finished..."}], "vocabulary_focus": ["dear", "hope", "finish", "exam", "hobby", "painting", "visit", "summer", "garden", "flower", "beautiful", "soon"], "common_mistakes": "学生常把现在完成时与一般过去时混淆。例如：'I have finished my exams yesterday' 是错误的，应改为 'I finished my exams yesterday' 或 'I have just finished my exams'。另外，信函末尾 'Love' 后应用逗号，不能漏掉。", "tags": ["letter", "family", "present perfect", "A2"], "author": ""}

{"full_text": "Dear Grandma,

Thank you very much for the birthday gift. The blue sweater is really beautiful! I like it a lot. It is warmer than my old one. I wore it to school yesterday, and my friends said it looked nice on me. I really like the color and the soft material.

Thank you also for the book about animals. I started reading it last night. It is more interesting than I expected. I learned a lot about penguins and dolphins.

I hope you are feeling well. Let's talk on the phone this weekend.

Love,
Tom", "translation": "亲爱的奶奶：

非常感谢您的生日礼物。那件蓝色毛衣真的很漂亮！我非常喜欢。它比我的旧毛衣更暖和。昨天我穿着它去学校，朋友们都说我穿起来很好看。我真的很喜欢它的颜色和柔软的面料。

也谢谢您送的那本关于动物的书。我昨晚开始读了。它比我想象的更有趣。我学到了很多关于企鹅和海豚的知识。

希望您身体很好。我们这周末通电话吧。

爱您的，
汤姆", "key_sentence_patterns": [{"pattern": "Thank you very much for...", "explanation": "用于表达感谢，后接名词或动词-ing形式。例：Thank you very much for the gift."}, {"pattern": "I really like...", "explanation": "表达强烈的喜欢。例：I really like the color."}, {"pattern": "It is warmer than...", "explanation": "形容词比较级结构，用于比较两个事物。例：It is warmer than my old one."}], "key_grammar": [{"point": "Thank you for + 名词/动名词", "example": "Thank you very much for the birthday gift. / Thank you also for sending the book."}, {"point": "形容词比较级", "example": "It is warmer than my old one. / It is more interesting than I expected."}, {"point": "一般过去时", "example": "I wore it to school yesterday. / My friends said it looked nice."}, {"point": "情态动词 'can' 表示能力", "example": "Let's talk on the phone."}], "vocabulary_focus": ["sweater", "beautiful", "warmer", "soft", "material", "interesting", "expected", "penguins", "dolphins", "weekend"], "common_mistakes": "学生在使用 'thank you for' 后容易误接动词原形，应改为动名词。例如：Thank you for give → Thank you for giving。另外，比较级中 'than' 前后结构需一致。", "tags": ["letter", "thank you", "birthday", "family", "A2"], "author": ""}

{"full_text": "Dear Mom and Dad,

Greetings from London! The weather is cold but sunny. We are having a wonderful time here. Tomorrow we are visiting the Tower of London. In the evening we are going to see a play. London is a very exciting city.

Yesterday we saw Big Ben and ate fish and chips. It was delicious! I am sending you this postcard from a small shop near the river.

I miss you both. See you soon!

Love,
Emma", "translation": "亲爱的爸爸妈妈：

来自伦敦的问候！天气寒冷但阳光明媚。我们在这里玩得很开心。明天我们要去参观伦敦塔。晚上我们打算去看一场戏。伦敦是一个令人兴奋的城市。

昨天我们看到了大本钟，还吃了炸鱼薯条。很好吃！我在河附近的一家小店里给你们寄这张明信片。

我想念你们。很快再见！

爱你们的，
艾玛", "key_sentence_patterns": [{"pattern": "We are having...", "explanation": "现在进行时表示正在发生的情况。例：We are having a wonderful time."}, {"pattern": "Tomorrow we are visiting...", "explanation": "用现在进行时表示将来的计划或安排。例：Tomorrow we are visiting the Tower of London."}, {"pattern": "See you soon!", "explanation": "用于告别，表示很快再见。例：See you soon!"}], "key_grammar": [{"point": "现在进行时表将来", "example": "We are visiting the Tower of London tomorrow. / We are going to see a play."}, {"point": "一般过去时", "example": "Yesterday we saw Big Ben and ate fish and chips."}, {"point": "表示地点的介词", "example": "from London / near the river / in the evening"}, {"point": "感叹句式（What ...）", "example": "What a wonderful time we have!"}], "vocabulary_focus": ["greetings", "wonderful", "visiting", "exciting", "delicious", "postcard", "river", "miss", "soon", "cold", "sunny"], "common_mistakes": "学生容易混淆现在进行时表将来和一般现在时表示计划。例如：'We are visiting tomorrow' 正确，但 'We visit tomorrow' 不自然。另外，'See you soon' 后常与 'I hope' 连用，但作为固定表达单独使用即可。", "tags": ["postcard", "travel", "London", "family", "A2"], "author": ""}

{"full_text": "I saw the wind today.
It pushed the clouds away.
It made the leaves dance fast,
A game that couldn't last.

I heard the wind last night.
It whispered, full of might.
"Why do you hide from me?
Come out and play with me!"

But when I looked around,
Not a sound could be found.
The wind had gone to play
In some far-away bay.", "translation": "我今天看到了风。
它把云朵推开了。
它让树叶快速舞动，
一场无法持久的游戏。

我昨晚听到了风。
它低语着，充满力量。
“你为什么躲着我？
出来和我玩吧！”

但当我环顾四周，
一点声音也找不到。
风已经去玩耍，
在某个遥远的海湾。", "key_sentence_patterns": [{"pattern": "I saw/heard the wind...", "explanation": "表达感官体验的句子，使用一般过去时描述所见所闻。"}, {"pattern": "It made the leaves dance fast.", "explanation": "make + 宾语 + 动词原形，表示‘使……做某事’，这里使用拟人手法。"}, {"pattern": "Why do you hide from me?", "explanation": "反问句，用‘why do you...’表达疑问或责备，这里风在说话，拟人化。"}, {"pattern": "Come out and play with me!", "explanation": "祈使句，用于邀请或命令，表达风的邀请。"}], "key_grammar": [{"point": "拟人化（Personification）", "example": "It whispered, full of might. — 把风比作会说话的人。"}, {"point": "反问句（Rhetorical question）", "example": "Why do you hide from me? — 并不期待回答，而是表达情感。"}, {"point": "押韵AABB", "example": "today/away, fast/last, night/might, me/me(注意第二段最后两行 me/me 是重复韵，但押韵结构为AABB：night/might, me/me；也可视为AA BB）"}, {"point": "一般过去时（Simple Past）", "example": "I saw, it pushed, it made, I heard, it whispered, I looked, could be found, had gone."}], "vocabulary_focus": ["wind", "pushed", "clouds", "leaves", "dance", "whispered", "might", "hide", "play", "found", "sound", "bay"], "common_mistakes": "学生容易混淆 'wind' 和 'wind'（卷绕/风）的发音；另外 'hide from me' 可能误写为 'hide me'。注意拟人化表达中动词使用第三人称单数（whispers 或 whispered）。", "tags": ["poem", "nature", "wind", "A2", "rhyme"], "author": "AI (Stevenson)"}

{"full_text": "In winter I get up at night
And dress by yellow candle-light.
In summer, quite the other way,
I have to go to bed by day.

I have to go to bed and see
The birds still hopping on the tree,
Or hear the grown-up people's feet
Still going past me in the street.

And does it not seem hard to you,
When all the sky is clear and blue,
And I should like so much to play,
To have to go to bed by day?", "translation": "冬天我夜里起床，
借着黄色的烛光亮。
夏天则完全相反，
我必须白天就上床。

我必须上床睡觉，却看到
小鸟还在树上蹦跳，
或者听到大人们的脚步
依旧在街上从我身旁走过。

难道你不觉得很难吗，
当天空晴朗蔚蓝，
而我多么想去玩耍，
却必须在白天上床睡觉？", "key_sentence_patterns": [{"pattern": "I have to go to bed by day.", "explanation": ""have to" 表示必须、不得不，强调客观需求。"}, {"pattern": "Does it not seem hard to you?", "explanation": "反问句，用 "Does it not..." 期待对方同意，表达感慨。"}, {"pattern": "I should like so much to play.", "explanation": ""should like" 是较礼貌的‘想要’，相当于 would like，表达愿望。"}], "key_grammar": [{"point": "一般现在时（Simple Present）", "example": "I get up, I have to go, I see, I hear, I should like."}, {"point": "have to + 动词原形", "example": "I have to go to bed by day. 表示外部强制或需要。"}, {"point": "押韵ABAB", "example": "night/light, way/day (第一段)；see/tree, feet/street (第二段)；you/blue, play/day (第三段) —— 严格交替押韵。"}, {"point": "反问句（Rhetorical question）", "example": "And does it not seem hard to you? 无需回答，强调观点。"}], "vocabulary_focus": ["winter", "summer", "night", "candle-light", "dress", "hop", "grown-up", "feet", "street", "clear", "blue", "play"], "common_mistakes": "学生容易把"have to"与"has to"混淆（主语I用have）；"does it not"在口语中常缩略为"doesn't it"，但这里为诗意保留完整形式；注意"should like"不是过去时，而是表示意愿。", "tags": ["poem", "childhood", "Stevenson", "A2", "rhyme"], "author": "Stevenson"}

{"full_text": "I have a little shadow that goes in and out with me,
And what can be the use of him is more than I can see.
He is very, very like me from the heels up to the head;
And I see him jump before me, when I jump into my bed.

The funniest thing about him is the way he likes to grow—
Not at all like proper children, which is always very slow;
For he sometimes shoots up taller like an India-rubber ball,
And he sometimes goes so little that there’s none of him at all.

He hasn’t got a notion of how children ought to play,
And can only make a fool of me in every sort of way.
He stays so close beside me, he’s a coward you can see;
I’d think shame to stick to nursie as that shadow sticks to me!", "translation": "我有一个小影子，跟我进进出出；
他有什么用处，我实在说不上来。
他从头到脚都和我一模一样；
我跳上床时，总看见他先我跳上去。

关于他最好笑的事，是他喜欢长大——
一点儿也不像正经孩子，总是慢慢长；
有时他长得像皮球一样飞快地蹿高，
有时他又缩得小小，完全不见了。

他根本不懂小孩子该怎么玩耍，
只会用各种方式捉弄我。
他紧紧跟在我身旁，你看他多胆小；\n我可羞于像他那样黏着保姆！", "key_sentence_patterns": [{"pattern": "I have a little shadow that goes in and out with me.", "explanation": "表示‘我有……，它……’的句型，用定语从句描述事物。"}, {"pattern": "He is very, very like me from the heels up to the head.", "explanation": "用‘from...to...’表示范围，强调相似性。"}, {"pattern": "I see him jump before me, when I jump into my bed.", "explanation": "用‘see + 宾语 + 动词原形’表示看见某人做某事，‘when’引导时间从句。"}, {"pattern": "He sometimes shoots up taller like an India-rubber ball.", "explanation": "用‘sometimes’表示频率，用‘like’进行比喻。"}], "key_grammar": [{"point": "现在进行时", "example": "He is growing. / I am jumping."}, {"point": "第三人称单数", "example": "He goes / He likes / He stays"}, {"point": "押韵 AABB", "example": "me/see, head/bed, grow/slow, ball/all, play/way, see/me"}], "vocabulary_focus": ["shadow", "use", "heels", "jump", "funniest", "grow", "proper", "shoots", "India-rubber ball", "notion", "coward", "nursie"], "common_mistakes": "学生容易混淆‘I see him jump’和‘I see him jumping’的区别。此处‘see + 动词原形’表示看见全过程，而‘seeing’表示看见正在进行。另外第三人称单数动词忘记加-s。", "tags": ["poem", "children", "Stevenson", "shadow", "playful", "A2"], "author": "Stevenson"}

cards.back: {"full_text": "Plants are living things. They need air, water, sunlight, and soil to grow. First, a seed is planted in the soil. The seed is small and brown. Then, the seed is watered. Water is absorbed by the seed. The seed starts to grow. After a few days, a small root comes out from the seed. The root goes down into the soil. It is used to take water and nutrients. Next, a stem grows up towards the sunlight. The stem is green and thin. It supports the leaves. Leaves are made by the plant. They are green and flat. Finally, flowers appear. Some flowers become fruits. The plant is now fully grown. Plants are very important. They give us food and oxygen. We should take care of them.", "translation": "植物是生物。它们需要空气、水、阳光和土壤才能生长。首先，种子被种在土壤里。种子又小又棕色。然后，种子被浇水。水被种子吸收。种子开始生长。几天后，从种子中长出一根小根。根向下伸入土壤。它被用来吸收水分和养分。接下来，茎朝着阳光向上生长。茎是绿色且细长的。它支撑着叶子。叶子由植物制造。它们是绿色且扁平的。最后，花朵出现。有些花朵会变成水果。植物现在已经完全长大。植物非常重要。它们给我们提供食物和氧气。我们应该照顾它们。", "key_sentence_patterns": [{"pattern": "First, ..., Then, ..., Finally, ...", "explanation": "表示顺序的句式，用于描述步骤或过程。"}, {"pattern": "It is used to + 动词原形", "explanation": "表示某物被用来做某事。"}, {"pattern": "Plants need ... to ...", "explanation": "表示植物需要某物来达到某个目的。"}], "key_grammar": [{"point": "被动语态（一般现在时）", "example": "A seed is planted. / Water is absorbed. / Leaves are made."}, {"point": "一般现在时", "example": "Plants need air. / The stem supports the leaves."}, {"point": "顺序连接词 First/Then/Finally", "example": "First, a seed is planted. {"full_text": "It was a beautiful Saturday morning, but Tom Sawyer was not happy. His aunt had given him a long task: he had to whitewash the entire fence. The fence was thirty yards long and nine feet high. Tom looked at it and felt very sad. He knew that other boys would come and laugh at him while he worked.

Soon, Ben Rogers walked by. He was eating an apple and making noises like a steamboat. He said to Tom, "You have to work, don't you?" Tom did not answer directly. Instead, he turned his brush and pretended to paint with great concentration. Then he said, "Work? Do you call this work? It's not every day that a boy gets to whitewash a fence."

Ben was surprised. He asked Tom if he could try painting too. Tom shook his head. He said that his aunt was very particular about the fence and that only he could do it properly. Ben begged harder. Finally, Tom agreed to let Ben paint a little, but he made Ben give him his apple first.

Tom sat in the shade, eating the apple and watching Ben work. Soon, other boys came. They all wanted to paint. By the end of the day, the fence had three coats of whitewash. Tom had collected a marble, a toy gun, and many other treasures. He had learned that making something seem difficult makes others want to do it for you.

He said to himself, "I made them do my work, and they even paid me for it!"", "translation": "那是一个美好的星期六早晨，但汤姆·索亚并不高兴。他的姨妈交给他一项冗长的任务：他必须把整道栅栏刷白。栅栏有三十码长、九英尺高。汤姆看着它，感到非常难过。他知道其他男孩会走过来，在他干活时嘲笑他。

不久，本·罗杰斯路过。他正吃着一个苹果，发出像蒸汽船一样的声音。他对汤姆说：“你得干活，是吧？”汤姆没有直接回答。相反，他转动刷子，假装非常专注地刷着。然后他说：“干活？你管这叫干活？不是每天都有人能得到刷栅栏的机会的。”

本很惊讶。他问汤姆他能不能也试着刷一下。汤姆摇了摇头。他说他的姨妈对栅栏的要求非常严格，只有他才能做好。本更加恳求了。最后，汤姆同意让本刷一点点，但前提是本先把他的苹果给他。

汤姆坐在阴凉处，吃着苹果，看着本干活。很快，其他男孩也来了。他们都想刷栅栏。到了晚上，栅栏已经刷了三层白浆。汤姆收集了一颗弹珠、一把玩具枪和许多其他宝贝。他明白了：让一件事看起来很难，别人就会抢着为你做。

他对自己说：“我让他们做了我的活儿，他们还付钱给我！”", "key_sentence_patterns": [{"pattern": "He had to whitewash the entire fence. cards.subject: english
cards.back:
{"full_text": "Alice was sitting on the bank of a river, feeling very bored. Her sister was reading a book that had no pictures or conversations. "What is the use of a book," Alice thought, "without pictures or conversations?"

Suddenly, a White Rabbit with pink eyes ran close by her. It was wearing a waistcoat and taking a watch out of its pocket. The Rabbit said, "Oh dear! Oh dear! I shall be too late!" Alice was very curious. She had never seen a rabbit with a pocket or a watch before. Without thinking, she jumped up and ran after it.

The Rabbit disappeared down a large rabbit hole. Alice did not stop. She followed it. The hole was as deep as a well. Alice found herself falling down, down, down. She fell slowly, as if she were floating. She looked around and saw cupboards and bookshelves on the sides of the hole. She wondered, "Was I ever going to reach the bottom?"

As she fell, she thought about many things. Could she see her cat Dinah at the bottom? Would the fall change her into someone else? The hole seemed as endless as a dream. Finally, she landed softly on a pile of dry leaves. The Rabbit was still running, and Alice ran after it into a long, low hall.

"What an adventure!" Alice said to herself. She was ready to see what was next. She had followed curiosity, and it had led her into a strange new world.", "translation": "爱丽丝正坐在河岸边，感到非常无聊。她的姐姐在读一本既没有图画也没有对话的书。“一本书有什么用，”爱丽丝想，“如果没有图画或对话？”

突然，一只粉红色眼睛的白兔从她身边跑过。它穿着一件背心，正从口袋里掏出一只怀表。兔子说：“哦，天哪！哦，天哪！我要迟到了！”爱丽丝非常好奇。她以前从未见过有口袋或怀表的兔子。她想都没想，跳起来追了上去。

兔子消失在了一个大兔子洞里。爱丽丝没有停下脚步。她跟着它掉了下去。那个洞像井一样深。爱丽丝发现自己往下落，往下落，往下落。她落得很慢，仿佛在漂浮。她环顾四周，看到洞壁两侧有橱柜和书架。她想知道：“我到底什么时候才能到达底部？”

在下落的过程中，她想了许多事情。她能在底部看到她的猫黛娜吗？这次坠落会不会把她变成别人？这个洞感觉像梦一样没有尽头。最后，她轻轻地落在一堆干树叶上。兔子还在跑，爱丽丝跟着它跑进了一个又长又低的大厅。

“多么奇妙的冒险！”爱丽丝对自己说。她准备好看看接下来会发生什么。她追随好奇心，而好奇心把她带入了一个陌生的新世界。", "key_sentence_patterns": [{"pattern": "The hole was as deep as a well. (as + adjective + as)", "explanation": "表示“像……一样……”，用于同级比较。"}, {"pattern": "Was I ever going to reach the bottom? (inverted question with 'was')", "explanation": "疑问句倒装结构，用于表达内心的疑问或不确定。"}, {"pattern": "Alice found herself falling down. (find oneself + doing something)", "explanation": "表示“发现自己正在做某事”，常用于描述无意中进入某种状态。"}], "key_grammar": [{"point": "过去进行时 (Past Continuous: was/were + -ing)", "example": "Alice was sitting on the bank. / The Rabbit was running."}, {"point": "疑问句倒装 (Inverted Questions in Reported Thoughts)", "example": "She wondered, "Was I ever going to reach the bottom?" (instead of 'I was going...')"}, {"point": "as...as... 结构 (Comparative structure)", "example": "as deep as a well / as endless as a dream"}], "vocabulary_focus": ["bank", "bored", "waistcoat", "pocket", "curious", "disappear", "cupboard", "bookshelf", "bottom", "float", "adventure", "curiosity"], "common_mistakes": "学生常混淆 as...as 和 so...as 的用法。肯定句中一般用 as...as，否定句可用 not as...as 或 not so...as。例如：正确是 'the hole was as deep as a well'，而不是 'the hole was so deep as a well'。另外，过去进行时中不要忘记助动词 was/were。", "tags": ["fantasy", "curiosity", "classic", "British", "adventure", "falling"], "author": "Lewis Carroll (adapted from Alice's Adventures in Wonderland)"}

cards.back: {"full_text": "Every afternoon, the children played in the Giant's garden. It was a large, lovely garden with soft green grass, beautiful flowers, and twelve peach trees. The birds sang so sweetly that the children often stopped their games to listen. But one day the Giant came back. He had been visiting his friend the Cornish Ogre for seven years. When he saw the children playing in his garden, he became very angry. 'What are you doing here?' he shouted. The children ran away. 'My garden is my own garden,' said the Giant. 'No one can play in it but me.' So he built a high wall around it and put up a sign: TRESPASSERS WILL BE PROSECUTED. He was a very selfish Giant. Then Spring came. Flowers appeared everywhere, and little birds flew around. But in the Giant's garden it was still winter. No birds came to sing, and the trees forgot to blossom. The Snow covered the grass, and the Frost painted the windows white. 'I do not understand why Spring is so late,' said the Giant as he looked out. But Spring and Summer never came. Only Autumn gave fruit to the garden, but the trees were empty. 'The Giant is too selfish,' said Autumn. So the garden was always winter. One morning the Giant heard beautiful music. A little bird was singing outside his window. Then he saw that children had entered the garden through a hole in the wall. They were sitting in the trees, and the trees were covered with blossoms. 'Spring has come at last!' said the Giant. He realized that he had been selfish. He went out into the garden. The children were frightened and ran away. Only one little boy did not run. He was too small, and tears were in his eyes. The Giant took him gently and put him in the tree. Then the tree burst into blossoms. The Giant knocked down the wall, and the children came back to play. 'It is your garden now, little children,' he said. And he played with them every day. He was not selfish anymore, and the garden became beautiful forever.", "translation": "每天下午，孩子们都会在巨人的花园里玩耍。那是一个又大又可爱的花园，有柔软的绿草、美丽的花朵和十二棵桃树。鸟儿唱得那么动听，孩子们常常停下游戏去听。但有一天，巨人回来了。他去看望他的朋友食人魔已有七年。当他看到孩子们在他的花园里玩耍时，他非常生气。“你们在这里干什么？”他喊道。孩子们都跑走了。“我的花园是我自己的花园，”巨人说，“除了我，谁也不能在里面玩。”于是他筑起一堵高墙，并贴了一块告示：擅入者将被追究责任。他是一个非常自私的巨人。春天来了，到处鲜花盛开，小鸟飞翔。但在巨人的花园里，却仍是冬天。没有鸟儿来唱歌，树木也忘了开花。白雪覆盖了草地，霜冻把窗户涂成了白色。“我不明白春天为什么来得这么晚，”巨人望着窗外说。但春天和夏天始终没有来。只有秋天给花园送来了果实，但树上却是空的。“巨人太自私了，”秋天说。于是花园里一直是冬天。一天早晨，巨人听到了美妙的音乐。一只小鸟正在他的窗外歌唱。然后他看见孩子们已从墙上的一个洞钻进花园。他们坐在树上，树上开满了花。“春天终于来了！”巨人说。他意识到自己一直很自私。他走进花园。孩子们吓坏了，纷纷跑开。只有一个小男孩没有跑。他太小了，眼睛里含着泪水。巨人轻轻地抱起他，把他放到树上。然后那棵树一下子开满了花。巨人推倒了墙，孩子们回来玩耍。“现在是你们的花园了，孩子们，”他说。从那天起他每天都和他们一起玩。他不再自私，花园也变得永远美丽。", "key_sentence_patterns": [{"pattern": "so...that...", "explanation": "如此……以至于……，用于表示因果或程度关系"}, {"pattern": "It is/was...that...", "explanation": "强调句式，用来强调某一部分"}, {"pattern": "No one can...but...", "explanation": "除了……没有人能……，表示唯一性"}], "key_grammar": [{"point": "条件状语从句 (if/when)", "example": "When he saw the children playing, he became angry."}, {"point": "关系从句 (who/which)", "example": "The children who had entered the garden were sitting in the trees."}, {"point": "not only...but also", "example": "The garden became not only beautiful but also happy forever."}], "vocabulary_focus": ["selfish", "trespasser", "prosecute", "blossom", "frost", "frighten", "gently", "burst", "knock down", "realize"], "common_mistakes": "学生在使用so...that时容易漏掉that；条件句when后常用现在时，但故事中需用过去时。", "tags": ["fairy tale", "generosity", "Oscar Wilde", "B1", "narrative"], "author": "Oscar Wilde"}

For eyes he had two bright sapphires, and a large red ruby glowed on his sword hilt. One night a little Swallow flew over the city. His friends had gone away to Egypt six weeks before, but he had stayed behind because he was in love with the most beautiful Reed. He had flown a long way and was very tired. He decided to sleep at the feet of the Happy Prince. As he put his head under his wing, a large drop of water fell on him. Another drop fell. He looked up and saw the Prince's eyes were full of tears. 'Why are you crying?' asked the Swallow. 'When I was alive,' said the Prince, 'I had a human heart, and I did not know what tears were. I lived in the Palace of Sans-Souci, where sorrow is not allowed. I was called the Happy Prince, and I was happy. Now I am dead, and they have set me up here so high that I can see all the ugliness and all the misery of my city. My heart is made of lead, but it cannot help crying. Far away there is a poor house. A woman is sewing, and her little boy is sick. He is thirsty, and his mother has no money to give him water. Swallow, little Swallow, will you take the ruby out of my sword and give it to her?' It was so cold that the Swallow had wanted to leave, but the Prince looked so sad that the little bird agreed. He took the ruby and dropped it into the woman's hand. Then he flew back. 'It is strange,' he said, 'but I feel quite warm now, although it is so cold.' 'That is because you have done a good deed,' said the Prince. The little Swallow began to think, and then he fell asleep.", "translation": "在高高的城市上空，一根高大的圆柱上，矗立着快乐王子的雕像。他全身贴满了薄薄的纯金叶片。他的眼睛是两颗明亮的蓝宝石，一颗大红宝石在他的剑柄上闪闪发光。一天晚上，一只小燕子飞过城市。他的朋友们六周前就去了埃及，但他却留了下来，因为他爱上了一株最美的芦苇。他飞了很远，非常疲倦。他决定在快乐王子的脚边睡觉。当他把头埋在翅膀下时，一大滴水落到了他身上。又一滴水落了下来。他抬头看见王子的眼里满是泪水。“你为什么哭？”燕子问道。“当我还活着的时候，”王子说，“我有一颗人类的心，不知道眼泪是什么。我住在无忧宫，那里不允许有悲伤。人们叫我快乐王子，我也确实很快乐。现在我死了，他们把我立得这么高，让我能看到城市里所有的丑陋和苦难。我的心是铅做的，却忍不住流泪。远处有一所穷人的房子。一个女人正在缝衣服，她的小男孩病了。他口渴，而他的母亲没钱给他水喝。燕子，小燕子，你能把我剑上的红宝石取下来送给她吗？”天那么冷，燕子本想离开，但王子看起来那么悲伤，小燕子就同意了。他取下红宝石，把它丢进那女人的手里。然后他飞了回来。“很奇怪，”他说，“虽然这么冷，我现在却觉得很温暖。”“那是因为你做了一件好事，”王子说。小燕子开始思考，然后便睡着了。", "key_sentence_patterns": [{"pattern": "It is/was so...that...", "explanation": "如此……以至于……，表示程度结果"}, {"pattern": "...cannot help doing...", "explanation": "忍不住做某事，表示无法控制的动作"}, {"pattern": "It is...that...", "explanation": "强调句式，强调某个成分"}], "key_grammar": [{"point": "过去完成时", "example": "His friends had gone away to Egypt six weeks before."}, {"point": "强调句 It was...that", "example": "It was the Prince who asked the Swallow to help."}, {"point": "too...to结构", "example": "The Swallow was too tired to fly farther."}], "vocabulary_focus": ["statue", "column", "gilded", "sapphire", "ruby", "swallow", "misery", "sew", "sick", "thirsty", "deed"], "common_mistakes": "学生常混淆过去完成时与一般过去时；强调句It was...that中易漏掉that；too...to结构后应用动词原形。", "tags": ["fairy tale", "compassion", "Oscar Wilde", "B1", "narrative"], "author": "Oscar Wilde"}

cards.back: {"full_text": "Rikki-tikki-tavi was a young mongoose. He lived with a family in a big house in India. One morning, while the family was having breakfast, Rikki-tikki was walking in the garden. He heard two snakes talking. They were Nag and Nagaina. Nag said, 'We must kill the people in the house. Then the garden will be ours.' Rikki-tikki felt very angry. He thought, 'I will protect my family!' He hid behind a flowerpot. When Nag came close, Rikki-tikki jumped. He bit Nag's head. Nag tried to throw him off, but Rikki-tikki held on, biting hard. The fight was dangerous. Finally, Nag became still. Rikki-tikki had won. But Nagaina was very angry. She came to the house, wanting to kill the boy. The boy was sitting on his bed. Rikki-tikki ran to save him. He shouted, 'Come here, you snake!' Nagaina hissed and moved quickly. Rikki-tikki jumped at her and bit her tail. She turned and bit him, but Rikki-tikki was faster. He bit her head. She escaped into her hole. Rikki-tikki followed her. The family waited, frightened. After some time, Rikki-tikki came out, tired but happy. Nagaina was dead. The family cheered. That night, Rikki-tikki slept on the boy's pillow. cards.back: {"full_text": "Della and Jim were a young couple who loved each other deeply. They lived in a small apartment and had very little money, but they had two special things: Della's beautiful long hair, which fell like a cascade of silk, and Jim's gold watch, a precious heirloom. It was Christmas Eve. Della wanted to buy a gift for Jim, but she had only one dollar and eighty-seven cents. She cried. 'If only I had more money!' she thought. Then she had an idea. She would sell her hair. So she went to a shop that bought hair and sold it for twenty dollars. With the money, she bought a platinum chain for Jim's watch. She was delighted. But when Jim came home, he saw Della's short hair. He was shocked. 'What happened to your hair?' he asked. Della explained that she had sold it to buy him a present. Jim laughed and gave her a small package. Inside were two beautiful combs that she had always wanted. Jim said, 'I sold my watch to buy the combs.' Della cried and smiled. They realized that their gifts were useless now, but their love was the greatest gift of all. They understood that if they had not sacrificed their treasures, they would not have shown their love so completely. cards.back: {"full_text": "The internet is a global system of connected computers. When you send a message or visit a website, your data is broken into small pieces called packets. These packets are sent through many different paths. Each packet contains information about where it came from and where it should go. Routers are special machines that decide which path a packet should take. If one path is busy or broken, the router will send the packet through another path. This makes the internet work even when part of it is damaged. All packets are put back together at the destination to form the original message. The internet uses a set of rules, which are called protocols. The most important protocol is TCP/IP. It ensures that data is sent correctly. For example, when you watch a video, the video data is divided into packets that travel to your device. Then your device uses the same rules to play the video. Without these rules, computers from different companies could not talk to each other. The internet was not created by one person. It was developed over many years by scientists and engineers. Today, if you connect to the internet, you can access information from all over the world. Then you can share your own ideas too.", "translation": "互联网是一个由连接起来的计算机组成的全球系统。当你发送消息或访问网站时，你的数据会被分解成称为数据包的小块。这些数据包通过许多不同的路径发送。每个数据包包含关于它从哪里来以及应该去哪里等信息。路由器是决定数据包走哪条路径的特殊机器。如果一条路径繁忙或损坏，路由器会通过另一条路径发送数据包。这使得互联网即使在部分受损时也能正常工作。所有数据包在目的地被重新组合成原始消息。互联网使用一套规则，这些规则被称为协议。最重要的协议是TCP/IP。它确保数据被正确发送。例如，当你观看视频时，视频数据被分割成数据包，这些数据包传输到你的设备。然后你的设备使用相同的规则播放视频。没有这些规则，来自不同公司的计算机就无法相互通信。互联网不是由一个人创建的。它是由科学家和工程师经过多年发展而来的。今天，如果你连接到互联网，你就可以访问来自世界各地的信息。然后你也可以分享你自己的观点。", "key_sentence_patterns": [{"pattern": "When you (do something), (something happens).", "explanation": "用于描述在某种条件下会发生什么。例如：'When you send a message or visit a website, your data is broken into small pieces.'"}, {"pattern": "If one path is (adjective), the router will (verb).", "explanation": "用于表示条件与结果。例如：'If one path is busy or broken, the router will send the packet through another path.'"}, {"pattern": "It ensures that (something happens).", "explanation": "用于说明某事物的作用。例如：'It ensures that data is sent correctly.'"}], "key_grammar": [{"point": "被动语态 (Passive Voice)", "example": "'your data is broken into small pieces' 和 'All packets are put back together'"}, {"point": "定语从句 which/that (Relative clauses with which/that)", "example": "'a set of rules, which are called protocols' 和 'packets that travel to your device'"}, {"point": "条件句 If..., then... (Conditional sentences with if)", "example": "'If one path is busy or broken, the router will send the packet through another path.'"}], "vocabulary_focus": ["internet", "system", "connected", "data", "packets", "routers", "path", "destination", "protocol", "device", "access", "share"], "common_mistakes": "学习者可能会混淆 'data' 和 'date'，或者忘记被动语态中 be 动词的形式。", "tags": ["technology", "internet", "B1", "informational"], "author": ""}

cards.back: {"full_text": "Pizza is one of the most popular foods in the world. Its history began in Italy, especially in the city of Naples. In the 18th century, flatbreads with toppings were sold by street vendors. These early pizzas were simple and cheap. They were eaten by poor people who needed a quick meal. The modern pizza was created in 1889. A baker named Raffaele Esposito was asked to make a special pizza for the king and queen of Italy. He made a pizza with tomatoes, mozzarella cheese, and basil. These ingredients, which are red, white, and green, represent the colors of the Italian flag. The pizza was called Margherita, after the queen. After that, pizza became more popular across Italy. Then Italian immigrants brought pizza to the United States in the early 20th century. In America, pizza changed. Both the crust and the toppings were adapted to local tastes. New styles, such as New York-style and Chicago deep-dish, were developed. Today, pizza is enjoyed everywhere. Both traditional Italian pizza and American-style pizza are loved by millions of people. The history of pizza shows that food can travel and change, but it always keeps its roots.", "translation": "比萨是世界上最受欢迎的食物之一。它的历史始于意大利，尤其是那不勒斯市。在18世纪，街头小贩会出售带配料的扁平面包。这些早期的比萨简单且便宜。它们被需要快速解决一餐的穷人食用。现代比萨是在1889年被创造出来的。一位名叫拉法埃莱·埃斯波西托的面包师被要求为意大利国王和王后制作一种特别的比萨。他制作了一个带有番茄、马苏里拉奶酪和罗勒的比萨。这些原料是红色、白色和绿色的，代表了意大利国旗的颜色。这个比萨被称为玛格丽特比萨，以王后的名字命名。在那之后，比萨在意大利变得更受欢迎。随后，意大利移民在20世纪初将比萨带到了美国。在美国，比萨发生了变化。饼皮和配料都根据当地口味进行了调整。新的风格，如纽约风格和芝加哥深盘风格，被发展出来。如今，比萨在世界各地都受到喜爱。传统的意大利比萨和美式比萨都被数百万人喜爱。比萨的历史表明，食物可以传播并发生变化，但它始终保留着自己的根源。", "key_sentence_patterns": [{"pattern": "(Something) was created / eaten / developed by (someone).", "explanation": "用于描述过去发生的被动动作，强调动作的承受者。例如：'The modern pizza was created in 1889.'"}, {"pattern": "Both (noun A) and (noun B) are (adjective/verb).", "explanation": "用于强调两个事物都具备某种属性。例如：'Both the crust and the toppings were adapted.'"}, {"pattern": "(Something) shows that (clause).", "explanation": "用于引出结论或说明。例如：'The history of pizza shows that food can travel and change.'"}], "key_grammar": [{"point": "被动语态（过去时） (Passive voice in past tense)", "example": "'They were eaten by poor people' 和 'The pizza was called Margherita'"}, {"point": "非限制性定语从句 (Non-restrictive relative clauses)", "example": "'These ingredients, which are red, white, and green, represent the colors of the Italian flag.'"}, {"point": "both...and... cards.back: {"full_text": "Many animals around the world are in danger of disappearing forever. These animals are called endangered species. Scientists estimate that thousands of species have become endangered in the last 100 years. As a result, many countries have created special laws to protect them. One major cause of endangerment is habitat loss. When forests are cut down or rivers are polluted, animals lose their homes. For example, the orangutan has lost most of its forest habitat in Southeast Asia because of palm oil plantations. Another serious problem is illegal hunting. Some people kill animals for their fur, horns, or bones. This has happened to rhinos and tigers. Climate change is also a growing threat. As temperatures rise, some animals might not be able to adapt quickly enough. Polar bears, for instance, could lose the sea ice they need for hunting. Conservation efforts have helped some species recover. The giant panda was once very endangered, but thanks to breeding programs, its population has increased. However, many challenges remain. If we do not act now, many more animals could disappear. It is important that we understand the problem and take action to protect wildlife.", "translation": "世界各地的许多动物都面临永远消失的危险。这些动物被称为濒危物种。科学家估计，在过去100年里，已有数千种物种濒临灭绝。因此，许多国家制定了专门的法律来保护它们。导致濒危的一个主要原因是栖息地丧失。当森林被砍伐或河流受到污染时，动物就失去了家园。例如，由于棕榈油种植园，苏门答腊猩猩已经失去了在东南亚的大部分森林栖息地。另一个严重的问题是非法狩猎。有些人为了获取动物的皮毛、角或骨头而猎杀它们。这种情况发生在犀牛和老虎身上。气候变化也是一个日益严重的威胁。随着气温上升，有些动物可能无法快速适应。例如，北极熊可能会失去它们捕猎所需的海冰。保护工作已经帮助一些物种恢复。大熊猫曾经非常濒危，但得益于繁殖计划，其数量已经增加。然而，许多挑战依然存在。如果我们现在不采取行动，更多动物可能会消失。我们必须理解这个问题并采取行动保护野生动物。", "key_sentence_patterns": [{"pattern": "Many animals are in danger of disappearing forever.", "explanation": "表示面临某种风险或危险的状态，'in danger of + 动名词' 意为 '有……的危险'。"}, {"pattern": "Animals called endangered species.", "explanation": "'called +名词' 用作过去分词短语作定语，意为 '被称为……的'。"}, {"pattern": "Scientists estimate that thousands of species have become endangered.", "explanation": "'estimate that + 从句' 表示 '估计……'，后面常跟 that 引导的宾语从句。"}, {"pattern": "If we do not act now, many more animals could disappear.", "explanation": "条件状语从句，'if... not...' 表示 '如果不……'，主句用情态动词 could 表示可能性。"}], "key_grammar": [{"point": "现在完成时 (Present Perfect)", "example": "Many species have become endangered in the last 100 years."}, {"point": "情态动词 might/could 表示可能性", "example": "Polar bears could lose the sea ice they need for hunting."}, {"point": "as a result 表示结果", "example": "As a result, many countries have created special laws to protect them."}], "vocabulary_focus": ["endangered", "species", "habitat", "conservation", "extinction", "pollution", "climate change", "illegal", "population", "adapt", "recover", "threat"], "common_mistakes": "学生容易混淆 'endangered'（濒危的）和 'extinct'（灭绝的），以及在使用现在完成时时忘记助动词 'have'。另外，'as a result' 容易被误写为 'as result'。", "tags": ["environment", "nature", "conservation", "wildlife", "endangered species"], "author": ""}

cards.back: {"full_text": "The solar system is made up of the Sun and everything that orbits around it. There are eight planets in our solar system. The four inner planets—Mercury, Venus, Earth, and Mars—are called terrestrial planets because they are rocky. The four outer planets—Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus, and Neptune—are called gas giants. Jupiter is the largest planet. It is about 11 times wider than Earth. Saturn, which is famous for its rings, is also very large. In fact, Saturn is almost as big as Jupiter. The Sun, however, is much larger than any planet. It is the center of the solar system and its gravity holds all the planets in orbit. Earth is the third planet from the Sun. It is the only planet known to have life. Water is found on Earth's surface, and the temperature is just right for living things. Mars is smaller than Earth and has a very thin atmosphere. In recent years, many space missions have been sent to Mars. They are designed to look for signs of past life. The solar system also includes dwarf planets, like Pluto, and many asteroids. Some asteroids are found in the asteroid belt between Mars and Jupiter. The planets are kept in their orbits by the Sun's gravity. Without gravity, the planets would fly off into space. Understanding the solar system helps us learn more about our own planet.", "translation": "太阳系由太阳以及围绕它运行的一切天体组成。我们的太阳系有八大行星。四颗内行星——水星、金星、地球和火星——被称为类地行星，因为它们由岩石构成。四颗外行星——木星、土星、天王星和海王星——被称为气态巨行星。木星是最大的行星，其宽度大约是地球的11倍。土星以它的环而闻名，也很大。事实上，土星几乎和木星一样大。然而，太阳比任何行星都大得多。它是太阳系的中心，其引力使所有行星保持在轨道上。地球是距离太阳第三近的行星，也是已知唯一有生命的行星。地球表面有液态水，温度也适宜生物生存。火星比地球小，大气层非常稀薄。近年来，许多太空任务被送往火星，旨在寻找过去生命的迹象。太阳系还包括矮行星（如冥王星）以及大量小行星。有些小行星位于火星和木星之间的小行星带。行星依靠太阳引力保持在轨道上。如果没有引力，行星就会飞向太空。了解太阳系有助于我们更好地认识自己的星球。", "key_sentence_patterns": [{"pattern": "The solar system is made up of the Sun and everything that orbits around it.", "explanation": "'be made up of' 意为 '由……组成'，后面的 'that' 引导定语从句修饰 'everything'。"}, {"pattern": "It is about 11 times wider than Earth.", "explanation": "用 'times + 比较级 + than' 表示倍数比较，意为 '是……的几倍'。"}, {"pattern": "Mars is smaller than Earth and has a very thin atmosphere.", "explanation": "'比较级 + than' 表示两者之间的比较，注意形容词比较级的变化。"}, {"pattern": "The planets are kept in their orbits by the Sun's gravity.", "explanation": "被动语态 'be + 过去分词 + by' 表示动作的承受者为主语，强调被谁或什么作用。"}], "key_grammar": [{"point": "比较级和最高级 (Comparative and Superlative)", "example": "Jupiter is the largest planet. / Mars is smaller than Earth."}, {"point": "倍数表达 (Multiples)", "example": "Jupiter is about 11 times wider than Earth."}, {"point": "被动语态 (Passive Voice)", "example": "The planets are kept in their orbits by the Sun's gravity."}], "vocabulary_focus": ["solar system", "planet", "orbit", "terrestrial", "gas giant", "gravity", "atmosphere", "surface", "temperature", "dwarf planet", "asteroid", "mission"], "common_mistakes": "学生容易混淆 'than' 和 'then'，以及忘记在比较级中使用 'than'。倍数表达时容易漏掉 'times' 或误用 'as...as' 结构。被动语态中 'by' 后面通常接动作的执行者，但有时会被省略。", "tags": ["space", "astronomy", "solar system", "planets", "science"], "author": ""}

cards.front: A Brief History of the Olympics
cards.subject: english
cards.back:
{"full_text": "The Olympic Games have a long and fascinating history. The first ancient Olympic Games were held in Olympia, Greece, in 776 BC. They were organized to honor the god Zeus and included only one event – a short running race. Over time, more sports were added, and athletes from all over Greece competed. The ancient Games were held every four years for almost 12 centuries. However, in 393 AD, they were stopped by the Roman emperor because of religious changes.

For nearly 1,500 years, there were no Olympic Games. Then, in the late 19th century, a Frenchman named Pierre de Coubertin revived the idea. He believed that sport could bring people together. The first modern Olympic Games were held in Athens in 1896, in the country where the ancient Games first began. Since then, the Olympics have been held every four years, except during the two World Wars.

The modern Games have grown a lot. New events have been added, and the number of participating countries has increased. In 1924, the first Winter Olympic Games were introduced. They take place in snowy locations where winter sports are possible. The Paralympics, for athletes with disabilities, were first organized in 1960. Since their beginning, the Paralympics have become a major international event.

Today, the Olympics are a symbol of peace and unity. They are watched by billions of people around the world. The spirit of the Games – “Faster, Higher, Stronger – Together” – continues to inspire athletes and spectators alike.", "translation": "奥林匹克运动会有着悠久而迷人的历史。第一届古代奥运会在公元前776年于希腊的奥林匹亚举行。它们是为了纪念宙斯神而举办的，最初只有一个项目——短跑比赛。随着时间的推移，增加了更多的运动项目，来自希腊各地的运动员都前来参加。古代奥运会每四年举行一次，持续了近12个世纪。然而，公元393年，由于宗教变革，罗马皇帝下令停止了这些比赛。

在近1500年的时间里，没有举办过奥运会。随后，在19世纪末，一位名叫皮埃尔·德·顾拜旦的法国人复兴了这一理念。他相信体育能够将人们团结在一起。第一届现代奥运会于1896年在雅典举行——正是在这个古老比赛最初起源的国家。自那时起，奥运会每四年举办一次，两次世界大战期间除外。

现代奥运会发展迅速。新增了许多项目，参赛国家数量也大幅增加。1924年，首届冬季奥运会问世。冬季奥运会在适合冬季运动的雪地地点举行。残奥会——为残疾运动员设立的赛事——于1960年首次组织。自创办以来，残奥会已成为一项重要的国际赛事。

cards.back: {"full_text": "Should school uniforms be required? This is a popular question among students, parents, and teachers. In my opinion, school uniforms are a good idea. They help create a fair and equal environment. When everyone wears the same clothes, there is less pressure to wear expensive brands. On the one hand, uniforms save time in the morning because students do not have to decide what to wear. They also make it easier for teachers to identify students and keep the school safe. On the other hand, some people say uniforms take away personal freedom. They believe students should be able to express themselves through clothing. However, I think there are other ways to show your personality, such as through your hobbies or how you talk to others. Schools should have a clear uniform policy, and students must follow it. This does not mean uniforms have to be boring. Many schools allow different colors or accessories. In conclusion, I believe school uniforms are helpful. They create a sense of community and reduce bullying about clothes. Therefore, I think schools should keep or start using uniforms.", "translation": "学校应该要求穿校服吗？这是学生、家长和老师中一个常见的问题。在我看来，校服是个好主意。它们有助于创造一个公平平等的环境。当每个人都穿同样的衣服时，穿昂贵品牌衣服的压力就小得多。一方面，校服节省了早上的时间，因为学生不需要决定穿什么。它们也让老师更容易识别学生并保持学校安全。另一方面，有些人说校服剥夺了个人自由。他们认为学生应该能够通过服装表达自己。然而，我认为还有其他方式可以展示个性，比如通过爱好或与人交谈的方式。学校应该有一个明确的校服政策，学生必须遵守。这并不意味着校服必须很无聊。许多学校允许不同颜色或配饰。总之，我认为校服是有帮助的。它们创造了社区感，减少了关于衣服的欺凌。因此，我认为学校应该保留或开始使用校服。", "key_sentence_patterns": [{"pattern": "In my opinion, ...", "explanation": "用于表达个人观点，意为“在我看来……”。"}, {"pattern": "On the one hand, ... cards.back: {"full_text": "Social media is a big part of our lives today. It is both good and bad, depending on how we use it. It is important that we understand the effects of social media. First, there are positive sides. Social media helps people stay connected with friends and family, even when they are far away. It also allows people to share news and ideas quickly. For example, you can learn about events in other countries in just a few seconds. However, social media also has negative effects. Although it can connect people, it can also make some people feel lonely or left out. Many people compare their lives with the perfect pictures they see online. This can cause stress and low self-esteem. Therefore, it is necessary that we use social media wisely. Even though it is fun to share and look at posts, we should take breaks and spend time offline. In conclusion, social media is a tool. Whether it is good or bad depends on how we use it. If we use it carefully, it can bring many benefits. But if we use it too much or without thinking, it can harm our mental health. We should always remember that real life is more important than online life.", "translation": "社交媒体如今是我们生活的重要组成部分。它既有好处也有坏处，取决于我们如何使用它。重要的是我们要理解社交媒体带来的影响。首先，有积极的一面。社交媒体帮助人们与远方的朋友和家人保持联系。它也让人快速分享新闻和想法。例如，你可以在几秒钟内了解其他国家的事件。然而，社交媒体也有负面影响。虽然它可以连接人们，但它也让一些人感到孤独或被冷落。许多人把自己和网上看到的完美照片进行比较。这可能导致压力和自卑。因此，明智地使用社交媒体是必要的。即使分享和浏览帖子很有趣，我们也应该休息一下，花时间离线。总之，社交媒体是一种工具。它是好是坏取决于我们如何使用它。如果我们谨慎使用，它可以带来很多好处。但如果我们过度使用或不经思考，它可能损害我们的心理健康。我们应该记住，现实生活比网络生活更重要。", "key_sentence_patterns": [{"pattern": "It is + 形容词 + that...", "explanation": "用于表达对某事的看法或评价，意为“……是很……的”。例如：It is important that we understand..."}, {"pattern": "Although / Even though + 从句, 主句", "explanation": "表示让步，意为“虽然……，但是……”。例如：Although it can connect people, it can also make some people feel lonely."}, {"pattern": "..., However, ... / ..., Therefore, ...", "explanation": "However 表示转折，Therefore 表示结果。用于连接观点，使论述更连贯。"}], "key_grammar": [{"point": "It is + adj + that 从句（形式主语）", "example": "It is important that we understand the effects of social media."}, {"point": "Although / Even though 引导的让步状语从句", "example": "Even though it is fun to share, we should take breaks."}, {"point": "连接副词 However 和 Therefore 的使用", "example": "However, social media also has negative effects. Therefore, it is necessary that we use social media wisely."}, {"point": "情态动词 should 表示建议", "example": "We should take breaks and spend time offline."}], "vocabulary_focus": ["social media", "effect", "positive", "negative", "connect", "lonely", "compare", "self-esteem", "wisely", "break", "mental health", "benefit"], "common_mistakes": "学生容易混淆 'Although' 和 'However' 的用法。'Although' 是连词，引导从句；'However' 是副词，通常放在句首并用逗号隔开。另外，'It is important that' 后面常常忘记使用虚拟语气（should + 动词原形），但在现代英语中也可直接用原形动词。", "tags": ["technology", "social media", "opinion", "B1"], "author": ""}

{"full_text": "Reading books is more than just a hobby. It is a powerful tool for learning and personal growth. In today's world, many people spend time on social media or watching videos. However, reading books offers benefits that these activities cannot provide.

First, reading improves your vocabulary and writing skills. When you read a book, you encounter new words and sentence structures. This helps you express yourself better. Not only does reading make you a better communicator, but it also helps you understand complex ideas.

Second, it is important to read books because they reduce stress. A good story can take you to another world. This escape from daily problems calms your mind and improves your mood. Studies show that just six minutes of reading can lower stress levels by 68 percent.

Third, reading helps you develop empathy. When you read about a character's life, you see the world from a different point of view. This makes you more understanding and kind towards others.

Finally, reading is good for your brain. It keeps your mind active and may prevent memory loss as you get older. Learning new things through reading creates new connections in your brain.

In conclusion, reading books is essential. Whether you read fiction or nonfiction, you gain knowledge, reduce stress, and become a better person. So pick up a book today and start reading!", "translation": "阅读书籍不仅仅是一种爱好。它是学习和个人成长的强大工具。在当今世界，很多人把时间花在社交媒体或观看视频上。然而，阅读书籍提供了这些活动无法提供的好处。

首先，阅读能提高你的词汇量和写作技巧。当你读一本书时，你会遇到新单词和句子结构。这有助于你更好地表达自己。阅读不仅使你成为更好的沟通者，还能帮助你理解复杂的想法。

其次，阅读书籍很重要，因为它能减轻压力。一个好故事可以带你到另一个世界。这种对日常问题的逃避能平静你的心，改善你的情绪。研究表明，仅仅六分钟的阅读就能将压力水平降低68%。

第三，阅读有助于培养同理心。当你读到角色的生活时，你会从不同的视角看世界。这让你对他人更加理解和友善。

最后，阅读对你的大脑有益。它让你的大脑保持活跃，并可能防止随着年龄增长而出现的记忆丧失。通过阅读学习新知识会在你的大脑中建立新的连接。

总之，阅读书籍是必不可少的。无论你读的是小说还是非小说，你都能获得知识、减轻压力，并成为一个更好的人。所以今天拿起一本书，开始阅读吧！", "key_sentence_patterns": [{"pattern": "Reading books is more than just...", "explanation": "读书不仅仅是……（强调超越表面意义）"}, {"pattern": "Not only does reading make you a better communicator, but it also helps you understand complex ideas.", "explanation": "阅读不仅使你成为更好的沟通者，还能帮助你理解复杂的想法。（not only...but also倒装结构）"}, {"pattern": "It is important to read books because they reduce stress.", "explanation": "读书很重要，因为它们能减轻压力。（It is important to do sth. 句型）"}, {"pattern": "Whether you read fiction or nonfiction, you gain knowledge...", "explanation": "无论你读小说还是非小说，你都能获得知识……（whether...or...引导让步状语从句）"}], "key_grammar": [{"point": "动名词作主语", "example": "Reading books is essential. (动名词短语作主语，谓语用单数)"}, {"point": "It is important to... (形式主语)", "example": "It is important to read books because they reduce stress. (It作形式主语，真正主语是to read books)"}, {"point": "not only...but also (倒装结构)", "example": "Not only does reading make you a better communicator, but it also helps you understand complex ideas. (not only位于句首时，主句部分倒装)"}, {"point": "比较级", "example": "Reading offers benefits that these activities cannot provide. (that引导定语从句，比较隐含)"}], "vocabulary_focus": ["hobby", "tool", "growth", "vocabulary", "stress", "empathy", "character", "prevent", "memory loss", "connection", "fiction", "nonfiction"], "common_mistakes": "学生容易混淆'reading books'和'read books'的用法：动名词作主语时用'Reading books is...'，而祈使句用'Read books!'；另外，'not only...but also'倒装时容易忘记将助动词提前（如'Not only does reading make...'而不是'Not only reading makes...'）。", "tags": ["reading", "opinion", "B1", "education", "personal development"], "author": ""}

{"full_text": "Space exploration is one of the most exciting and important fields of science today. Some people argue that we should spend money on problems on Earth instead. However, I believe that exploring space brings great benefits to everyone.

First, it is argued that space exploration leads to new technologies. Many inventions we use every day came from space programs. For example, satellite technology is used for weather forecasting, GPS, and communication. If we had never explored space, these technologies would not exist. They make our lives safer and more convenient.

Second, space exploration helps us understand our own planet. By studying other planets, scientists learn more about climate change and natural disasters. This knowledge can be used to protect the Earth. For instance, satellites are used to monitor deforestation and ocean pollution.

Third, space exploration inspires young people to study science and engineering. When students see astronauts and rockets, they become excited about STEM subjects. This creates a new generation of scientists who will solve future problems.

Of course, space programs are expensive. But the money spent on space is not wasted. It creates jobs and drives innovation. Moreover, if we stopped exploring space, we would lose the chance to discover new resources and even new places to live in the future.

In conclusion, space exploration is a wise investment. It improves technology, protects our planet, and inspires the next generation. We should continue to support it. After all, the future of humanity depends on our ability to explore the unknown.", "translation": "太空探索是当今最激动人心、最重要的科学领域之一。一些人认为我们应该把钱花在地球上的问题上。然而，我相信探索太空给每个人都带来了巨大的好处。

首先，有人认为太空探索带来了新技术。我们每天使用的许多发明都来自太空计划。例如，卫星技术用于天气预报、GPS和通信。如果我们从未探索过太空，这些技术就不会存在。它们使我们的生活更安全、更便利。

其次，太空探索有助于我们了解自己的星球。通过研究其他行星，科学家们更多地了解了气候变化和自然灾害。这些知识可用于保护地球。例如，卫星用于监测森林砍伐和海洋污染。

第三，太空探索激励年轻人学习科学和工程。当学生看到宇航员和火箭时，他们对STEM科目变得兴奋。这创造了一代新的科学家，他们将解决未来的问题。

当然，太空计划是昂贵的。但花在太空上的钱并没有被浪费。它创造了就业并推动创新。此外，如果我们停止探索太空，我们将失去发现新资源甚至未来新居住地的机会。

总之，太空探索是一项明智的投资。它改善技术、保护我们的星球，并激励下一代。我们应该继续支持它。毕竟，人类的未来取决于我们探索未知的能力。", "key_sentence_patterns": [{"pattern": "It is argued that space exploration leads to new technologies.", "explanation": "有人认为太空探索带来了新技术。（It is argued that... 被动语态表达观点）"}, {"pattern": "If we had never explored space, these technologies would not exist.", "explanation": "如果我们从未探索过太空，这些技术就不会存在。（与过去事实相反的虚拟语气）"}, {"pattern": "The money spent on space is not wasted.", "explanation": "花在太空上的钱并没有被浪费。（过去分词短语作后置定语）"}, {"pattern": "We should continue to support it.", "explanation": "我们应该继续支持它。（should表示建议）"}], "key_grammar": [{"point": "虚拟语气 (if + 过去完成时, would + 现在完成时)", "example": "If we had never explored space, these technologies would not exist. (与过去事实相反的假设)"}, {"point": "It is argued that... (被动语态表达观点)", "example": "It is argued that space exploration leads to new technologies. (形式主语it，真正主语为that从句)"}, {"point": "被动语态的一般现在时和现在完成时", "example": "Satellites are used to monitor deforestation. (一般现在时被动)；The money spent on space is not wasted. (过去分词spent作定语，is wasted被动)"}, {"point": "情态动词should表示建议", "example": "We should continue to support it."}], "vocabulary_focus": ["exploration", "field", "benefit", "satellite", "forecasting", "climate change", "disaster", "inspire", "astronaut", "STEM", "innovation", "investment", "humanity"], "common_mistakes": "学生在使用虚拟语气时容易混淆时态：与过去事实相反时，从句用had done，主句用would have done（本句中would exist是虚拟现在，但实际是与过去相反，正确应为would exist表示对现在的影响）；另外，'It is argued that...'中that从句的谓语时态需与主句一致，但也要根据逻辑调整。", "tags": ["space", "science", "opinion", "B1", "technology"], "author": ""}

March 15, 2025

Ms. Jane Johnson
Human Resources Manager
TechSolutions Inc.
456 Oak Avenue
Chicago, IL 60601

Dear Ms. Johnson,

I am writing to apply for the position of Junior Software Developer, which was advertised on your company website last week. I have always admired TechSolutions Inc. for its innovative work in the technology industry, and I would be honored to join your team.

I recently graduated from Springfield University with a Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science. During my studies, I gained strong skills in programming languages such as Python and Java. I also have experience in working on team projects, where I developed problem-solving and communication abilities. Last summer, I completed an internship at a local tech company, where I helped create a mobile application for inventory management.

In addition to my technical skills, I am a quick learner and a dedicated team player. I believe that my experience and enthusiasm make me a suitable candidate for this position.

I have attached my resume and a letter of recommendation. I would be grateful if you could consider my application. I am available for an interview at your convenience. Thank you for your time and consideration.

Sincerely,

(Your Signature)

David Chen", "translation": "123 Main 街

简·约翰逊女士

TechSolutions 公司
456 橡树大道
芝加哥，伊利诺伊州 60601

尊敬的约翰逊女士：

我写信是为了申请初级软件开发者的职位，该职位上周在贵公司网站上发布。我一直钦佩 TechSolutions 公司在科技行业的创新工作，若能加入贵团队，我将不胜荣幸。

我最近从斯普林菲尔德大学毕业，获得了计算机科学学士学位。学习期间，我掌握了 Python 和 Java 等编程语言的扎实技能。我也有参与团队项目的经验，锻炼了解决问题和沟通的能力。去年夏天，我在一家当地科技公司完成了实习，协助开发了一款用于库存管理的移动应用程序。

除了技术技能外，我学习能力强，且是尽职的团队合作者。我相信我的经验和热情使我成为这一职位的合适人选。

随信附上我的简历和一封推荐信。如您能考虑我的申请，我将不胜感激。我可以在您方便的时间参加面试。感谢您抽出时间审阅。

此致

I tried to contact your support team by phone, but I was kept on hold for over 30 minutes. When I finally spoke to someone, they told me to send an email instead. This was very frustrating.

I would appreciate it if you could replace the blender or give me a full refund. According to your return policy, faulty products can be returned within 30 days. I have kept the original box and all accessories. Please let me know what you need from me to process this request.

Thank you for your understanding. I look forward to your reply.

Sincerely,

cards.back: {"full_text": "Nelson Mandela was born in 1918 in a small village in South Africa. He grew up in a country where black people did not have the same rights as white people. This system was called apartheid. Mandela decided to fight against it. At first, he used peaceful protests, but the government did not listen. He then helped to start a military group, which led to his arrest in 1962. He was sentenced to life in prison. During his 27 years in prison, Mandela continued to be a symbol of resistance. Many people around the world called for his release. When he was finally freed in 1990, he did not ask for revenge. Instead, he worked with his former enemies to build a new South Africa. In 1994, he became the first black president of the country. He had spent his whole life fighting for equality, and he never gave up. Mandela once said, \"Education is the most powerful weapon which you can use to change the world.\" He died in 2013, but his legacy lives on. People who admired him remember him as a man of courage and forgiveness.", "translation": "纳尔逊·曼德拉1918年出生于南非一个小村庄。他在一个黑人没有与白人同等权利的国家长大，这个体系被称为种族隔离。曼德拉决定与之抗争。起初他采用和平抗议，但政府不听。于是他协助组建了一个军事组织，这导致他在1962年被捕，并被判处终身监禁。在监狱的27年里，曼德拉一直是抵抗的象征。世界各地许多人呼吁释放他。1990年他终于获释时，并没有寻求报复，而是与昔日的敌人合作建设新南非。1994年，他成为南非首位黑人总统。他一生为平等而奋斗，从未放弃。曼德拉曾说：“教育是改变世界的最强大武器。”他于2013年去世，但遗产永存。敬佩他的人们记得他是一位勇敢且宽恕的人。", "key_sentence_patterns": [{"pattern": "He grew up in a country where black people did not have the same rights.", "explanation": "用‘where’引导定语从句修饰地点，表示‘在……的国度里’。"}, {"pattern": "The government did not listen, which led to his arrest.", "explanation": "用‘which’引导非限制性定语从句，指代前面整个句子。"}, {"pattern": "When he was finally freed, he did not ask for revenge.", "explanation": "用‘When’引导时间状语从句，表示‘当……时’。"}, {"pattern": "He had spent his whole life fighting for equality.", "explanation": "用‘had spent’（过去完成时）表示在过去某个时间之前已经完成的动作。"}, {"pattern": "People who admired him remember him as a man of courage.", "explanation": "用‘who’引导定语从句修饰人。"}], "key_grammar": [{"point": "过去时 vs 过去完成时", "example": "He was born in 1918. (一般过去时) / He had spent his whole life fighting before he became president. (过去完成时表示过去的过去)"}, {"point": "时间状语从句", "example": "When he was finally freed in 1990, he did not ask for revenge."}, {"point": "定语从句 who/whom", "example": "People who admired him remember him. / He was a man whom many respected. (文中未出现whom，但可扩展)"}], "vocabulary_focus": ["apartheid", "rights", "protest", "military", "arrest", "sentence", "prison", "symbol", "release", "revenge", "equality", "legacy"], "common_mistakes": "学生易混淆一般过去时与过去完成时。例如，若说‘He spent his whole life fighting’是正确的过去时，但若要表达在他成为总统前已完成，需用过去完成时。另外，定语从句中‘who’和‘which’的区分需注意：人用who，物用which。", "tags": ["biography", "Nelson Mandela", "courage", "apartheid", "equality", "B1", "history"], "author": ""}

cards.back: {"full_text": "Last Friday, our school held its annual Sports Day. The weather was perfect, and all students from Year 7 to 11 took part in various events. The day began with a parade of athletes, led by the school band. While the runners were preparing for the 100-metre race, teachers were setting up the long jump area. The highlight was the relay race, which was won by Class 9B after a close finish. Many records were broken during the track events. For example, the 400-metre record was improved by Sarah Lee, who finished in just 56 seconds. Her performance was praised by everyone. Meanwhile, field events like shot put and high jump were also taking place. In the afternoon, the results were announced, and medals were given to the winners. The event was considered a great success. Students were encouraged to participate more in future sports activities. A photo of the winning team was taken for the school website. The day ended with a short speech from the head teacher, who thanked all the volunteers and staff. Overall, it was a memorable day for the whole school.", "translation": "上周五，我们学校举行了年度运动会。天气非常完美，7到11年级的所有学生都参加了不同的项目。这一天以运动员游行开始，由学校乐队领队。当跑步选手准备100米赛跑时，老师们正在布置跳远区域。最精彩的部分是接力赛，九班在激烈竞争后赢得了比赛。许多记录在径赛项目中被打破。例如，400米纪录被莎拉·李提高，她仅用56秒完成。她的表现受到了大家的赞扬。与此同时，像铅球和跳高这样的田赛项目也在进行。下午，结果被宣布，奖牌被颁发给获胜者。这次活动被认为是非常成功的。学生们被鼓励以后更多地参加体育活动。获胜队伍的照片被拍下放在了学校网站上。这一天以校长的简短讲话结束，他感谢了所有志愿者和工作人员。总的来说，这对整个学校来说是一个难忘的日子。", "key_sentence_patterns": [{"pattern": "The highlight was [noun phrase], which [past tense verb].", "explanation": "用于强调事件中最精彩的部分，后面用which从句补充说明。"}, {"pattern": "While [subject] was/were [verb-ing], [subject] was/were [verb-ing].", "explanation": "描述两个同时发生的过去进行动作。"}, {"pattern": "[Something] was [past participle] by [someone].", "explanation": "被动语态结构，强调动作的承受者。"}], "key_grammar": [{"point": "过去进行时 (Past Continuous)", "example": "While the runners were preparing for the race, teachers were setting up the long jump area."}, {"point": "被动语态 (Passive Voice)", "example": "Many records were broken during the track events."}, {"point": "The highlight was... (强调结构)", "example": "The highlight was the relay race, which was won by Class 9B."}], "vocabulary_focus": ["annual", "parade", "athletes", "relay", "record", "improved", "performance", "praised", "field events", "announced", "medals", "memorable"], "common_mistakes": "混淆过去进行时和一般过去时：不要用 'While the runners prepared' 代替 'While the runners were preparing'，因为强调正在进行的动作。被动语态中漏掉 'by'：例如 'was praised everyone' 应为 'was praised by everyone'。", "tags": ["school", "sports day", "report", "event", "B1"], "author": ""}

cards.back: {"full_text": "A new community park has been opened in the city centre. According to the mayor, the park was designed to provide a green space for families and children. Construction started last year and was completed in just ten months. The park includes a large playground, a jogging track, and several benches. Trees and flowers have been planted around the area to make it more attractive. According to local residents, the opening ceremony was held last Saturday. Many people attended and enjoyed the free activities. The park will be open every day from 6 a.m. to 9 p.m. Visitors are reminded to keep the park clean and follow the rules. So far, the park has been visited by more than five thousand people. The project was funded by the government and local businesses. In the future, more facilities, such as a small cafe, may be added. According to the city council, this park is the first of several planned green spaces. Residents have expressed their satisfaction with the new park, saying it is a great place to relax and exercise.", "translation": "一个新的社区公园已在市中心开放。据市长称，这个公园旨在为家庭和儿童提供绿色空间。建设从去年开始，仅用了十个月就完工了。公园包括一个大型游乐场、一条慢跑道和几张长椅。树木和花卉已被种植在周围区域，使其更具吸引力。据当地居民说，开幕仪式于上周六举行。许多人参加并享受了免费活动。公园每天从早上6点开放到晚上9点。游客被提醒要保持公园清洁并遵守规则。到目前为止，已有超过5000人参观了这个公园。该项目由政府和企业资助。未来可能会增加更多设施，比如一个小咖啡馆。据市议会称，这个公园是计划中的几个绿色空间中的第一个。居民们对新公园表示满意，称其是一个放松和锻炼的好地方。", "key_sentence_patterns": [{"pattern": "According to [person/organization], [sentence].", "explanation": "表示信息的来源，常用于新闻报道。"}, {"pattern": "[Something] has been [past participle] [time phrase].", "explanation": "现在完成时的被动语态，强调动作已经完成并对现在有影响。"}, {"pattern": "[Subject] will be [verb] every day from [time] to [time].", "explanation": "一般将来时的被动语态，表示按计划发生的事。"}], "key_grammar": [{"point": "被动语态 (Passive Voice) - 现在完成时", "example": "A new community park has been opened in the city centre."}, {"point": "被动语态 (Passive Voice) - 一般过去时", "example": "The park was designed to provide a green space."}, {"point": "引语 (Reported speech) - According to...", "example": "According to the mayor, the park was designed to provide a green space."}], "vocabulary_focus": ["community", "designed", "construction", "completed", "playground", "jogging track", "planted", "ceremony", "attended", "funded", "facilities", "satisfaction"], "common_mistakes": "使用 'According to' 后直接跟从句时忘记主句：例如 'According to the mayor, the park was designed' 正确，不要写成 'According to the mayor, the park designed'。现在完成时被动语态中漏掉 'been'：如 'has opened' 应为 'has been opened'。", "tags": ["news", "park", "community", "local", "report", "B1"], "author": ""}

{"full_text": "Two roads diverged in a yellow wood,
And sorry I could not travel both
And be one traveler, long I stood
And looked down one as far as I could
To where it bent in the undergrowth;

Then took the other, as just as fair,
And having perhaps the better claim,
Because it was grassy and wanted wear;
Though as for that the passing there
Had worn them really about the same,

And both that morning equally lay
In leaves no step had trodden black.
Oh, I kept the first for another day!
Yet knowing how way leads on to way,
I doubted if I should ever come back.

I shall be telling this with a sigh
Somewhere ages and ages hence:
Two roads diverged in a wood, and I—
I took the one less traveled by,
And that has made all the difference.", "translation": "黄树林里分叉两条路，
可惜我不能同时涉足。
我久久伫立，向着一条路极目望去，
直到它蜿蜒在灌木丛中消失；

然后选了另一条，同样美丽，
或许更有吸引力，
因为它绿草如茵，需要被踩踏；
虽然就实际而言，
来往的足迹其实相差无几。

那天清晨两条路都铺满落叶，
尚未被脚步踏黑。
哦，我把第一条留待他日！
但深知道路连绵无尽，
我怀疑自己能否再返回。

多年后我将带着叹息讲述：
树林里分出两条路，而我——
我选择了人迹更少的那条，

cards.front: Stopping by Woods on a Snowy Evening
cards.subject: english
cards.back:
{"full_text": "Whose woods these are I think I know.
His house is in the village though;
He will not see me stopping here
To watch his woods fill up with snow.

My little horse must think it queer
To stop without a farmhouse near
Between the woods and frozen lake
The darkest evening of the year.

He gives his harness bells a shake
To ask if there is some mistake.
The only other sound’s the sweep
Of easy wind and downy flake.

The woods are lovely, dark and deep,
But I have promises to keep,
And miles to go before I sleep,
And miles to go before I sleep.", "translation": "我想我知道这是谁的树林。
他的房子就在村里；
他不会看到我在此停留
欣赏他的树林落满雪。

我的小马一定觉得奇怪
为何停在无人的农舍附近
在树林和冰冻的湖泊之间
在一年中最黑暗的夜晚。

它摇了摇马具的铃铛
询问是否出了差错。
除此以外只有微风的轻拂
和轻柔雪花的飘落。

树林美丽、幽暗而深邃，
但我有诺言要遵守，
还有长路要走才能安睡，
还有长路要走才能安睡。", "key_sentence_patterns": [{"pattern": "Whose woods these are I think I know.", "explanation": "疑问词Whose引导的从句作宾语，主句主语I后置——属于陈述语序的宾语从句。"}, {"pattern": "He will not see me stopping here", "explanation": "see + 宾语 + 现在分词，表示'看见某人正在做某事'。"}, {"pattern": "To ask if there is some mistake", "explanation": "动词不定式表目的（为了询问），if引导宾语从句。"}, {"pattern": "And miles to go before I sleep", "explanation": "to go修饰miles，表示'还有……要走'；before引导时间状语从句。该句重复强调。"}], "key_grammar": [{"point": "疑问句作宾语从句（疑问词+陈述语序）", "example": "Whose woods these are I think I know. — 正常语序为I think I know whose woods these are。"}, {"point": "拟人化（personification）", "example": "My little horse must think it queer — 马被赋予人的思考能力。"}, {"point": "押韵AABA（rhyme scheme）", "example": "第一诗节：know, though, here, snow — 押韵模式为AABA（第三行不押韵）。"}, {"point": "省略与简写（contraction）", "example": "sound’s = sound is, 口语化的缩写。"}], "vocabulary_focus": ["woods", "queer", "harness", "sweep", "downy", "flake", "lovely", "deep", "promises", "miles"], "common_mistakes": "第一行'Whose woods these are I think I know'为倒装或宾语前置，学习者常误以为是疑问句而加问号。事实上这是一个陈述句（句末为句号），意思是'我知道这是谁的树林'。", "tags": ["poem", "nature", "winter", "Robert Frost", "contemplation"], "author": "R. {"full_text": "Dear Editor,

I have read your recent article about improving our community and I want to add my voice. I am writing to express my concern about the lack of public benches in our neighborhood. Many elderly residents have no place to sit and rest when they go for a walk. This is a serious problem because it makes it difficult for them to enjoy the outdoors and stay active. I am not alone in this opinion; many of my neighbors agree.

Last week, I saw an old woman sitting on the ground because she was tired. Her legs hurt and she needed a break. This situation is not acceptable in a modern city. Other cities have many benches in parks and along streets. Why can't our city do the same? Benches are simple and cheap but they make a big difference.

I think the local government should install more benches in public areas. They are not expensive and they help people of all ages. Children can sit while playing, adults can rest after shopping, and elderly people can take breaks during their walks. Benches also encourage social interaction. People can meet and talk while sitting.

Furthermore, benches improve the appearance of the neighborhood. A park with benches looks more welcoming. I hope you will publish this letter and bring attention to this issue. Thank you for your time.

Sincerely,
A Concerned Resident", "translation": "尊敬的编辑：

我阅读了您最近关于改善社区的文章，也想表达我的看法。我写这封信是想表达我对我们街区缺乏公共长椅的担忧。许多老年居民散步时没有地方可以坐下休息。这是一个严重的问题，因为它让他们难以享受户外活动和保持活力。我并不是唯一有这种想法的人，我的许多邻居也同意。

上周，我看到一位老妇人因为累了坐在地上。她的腿疼，需要休息一下。这种情况在一个现代化城市中是不可接受的。其他城市在公园和街道旁都有很多长椅。为什么我们的城市不能这样做呢？长椅简单又便宜，但作用很大。

我认为当地政府应该在公共区域安装更多长椅。它们不贵，而且能帮助各个年龄段的人。孩子们可以边玩边坐，成年人购物后可以休息，老年人散步时可以歇脚。长椅还能促进社交互动，人们可以坐着见面聊天。

此外，长椅能改善社区面貌。有长椅的公园看起来更宜人。我希望您能刊登这封信，引起对这一问题的关注。感谢您的时间。

此致
一位关心的居民", "key_sentence_patterns": [{"pattern": "I am writing to express my concern about...", "explanation": "Use this pattern to begin a letter and state the main issue you want to discuss."}, {"pattern": "I think [subject] should [verb]...", "explanation": "Use this to give an opinion or make a suggestion."}, {"pattern": "Why can't [subject] do [something]?", "explanation": "Use this rhetorical question to emphasize a point or express frustration."}], "key_grammar": [{"point": "Present perfect for recent experiences or actions", "example": "I have read your recent article. / I have seen an old woman sitting on the ground."}, {"point": "Modal verb 'should' for suggestions", "example": "I think the local government should install more benches."}, {"point": "Simple past for specific past events", "example": "Last week, I saw an old woman sitting on the ground."}], "vocabulary_focus": ["residents", "benches", "elderly", "neighborhood", "install", "encourage", "social interaction", "appearance", "welcoming", "publish"], "common_mistakes": ["Incorrect: 'I am agree' → Correct: 'I agree'", "Incorrect: 'I am concern about' → Correct: 'I am concerned about'", "Incorrect: 'make difference' → Correct: 'make a difference'", "Incorrect: 'benefits' as verb singular → Correct: 'benefit' (e.g., 'They benefit people')"], "tags": ["social issue", "letter", "B1", "community", "urban planning"], "author": "Original"}

She was the first woman to win a Nobel Prize. Marie Curie died in 1934. Her discoveries helped many scientists after her. Today, Marie Curie is still remembered as a pioneer in science. She showed that women can be great scientists too.", "translation": "玛丽·居里是一位著名的科学家。她于1867年出生在波兰。她移居法国，在巴黎大学学习。在大学里，她遇到了一位名叫皮埃尔·居里的科学家，他们结婚了。他们一起研究放射性。玛丽·居里发现了两种新元素：钋和镭。她制造了特殊的仪器来测量辐射。她的工作对医学非常重要。后来，她获得了两次诺贝尔奖。一次是1903年的物理学奖，另一次是1911年的化学奖。她是第一位获得诺贝尔奖的女性。玛丽·居里于1934年去世。她的发现帮助了许多后来的科学家。如今，玛丽·居里仍然作为科学先驱被人们铭记。她证明了女性也可以成为伟大的科学家。", "key_sentence_patterns": [{"pattern": "She was born in [year] in [place].", "explanation": "Used to introduce someone's birth year and place."}, {"pattern": "She discovered [something].", "explanation": "Used to state a scientific discovery."}, {"pattern": "She is remembered as [a/an] [noun].", "explanation": "Used to describe how someone is known historically."}], "key_grammar": [{"point": "Past simple tense for completed actions", "example": "Marie Curie discovered two new elements."}, {"point": "Passive voice", "example": "She is still remembered as a pioneer."}, {"point": "Present perfect with 'still'", "example": "Today, Marie Curie is still remembered."}], "vocabulary_focus": ["pioneer", "discover", "radiation", "element", "Nobel Prize", "measure", "research"], "common_mistakes": "Using present simple instead of past simple for completed historical events (e.g., 'She discovers radium' instead of 'She discovered radium').", "tags": ["science", "biography", "women in science", "Nobel Prize", "radiation"], "author": "Original"}

{"full_text": "Steve Jobs was born in 1955 in California. He was adopted as a baby and grew up in Silicon Valley. As a teenager, he became interested in electronics and met Steve Wozniak, a computer expert. In 1976, Jobs and Wozniak founded Apple Computer in Jobs's garage. They created the Apple I, a simple computer for hobbyists. The Apple II, released later, became very popular and made Apple a successful company.

In 1985, after a conflict with the board of directors, Jobs left Apple. He started a new company called NeXT, which made powerful computers for education and business. NeXT was not a big commercial success, but its technology was very advanced. During this time, Jobs also bought a small animation studio from George Lucas. He renamed it Pixar. Pixar created the first fully computer-animated film, Toy Story, in 1995. The film was a huge success, and Pixar became a major player in Hollywood.

In 1997, Apple bought NeXT, and Jobs returned to the company as CEO. He brought new ideas and a focus on design. Under his leadership, Apple launched the iMac, iPod, iPhone, and iPad. These products changed the way people use technology. Jobs was known for his perfectionism and his vision. He believed in making products that were simple, beautiful, and easy to use.

Steve Jobs died in 2011 after a long battle with cancer. His legacy lives on in the products we use every day. He showed that one person's imagination can change the world.", "translation": "史蒂夫·乔布斯于1955年出生于加利福尼亚州。他出生后被收养，在硅谷长大。十几岁时，他对电子学产生了兴趣，并结识了电脑专家史蒂夫·沃兹尼亚克。1976年，乔布斯和沃兹尼亚克在乔布斯的车库里创立了苹果电脑公司。他们制造了Apple I，这是一款面向爱好者的简单电脑。后来发布的Apple II非常受欢迎，使苹果成为一家成功的公司。

{"full_text": "True! — nervous — very, very dreadfully nervous I had been and am; but why will you say that I am mad? The disease had sharpened my senses — not destroyed — not dulled them. Above all was the sense of hearing acute. I heard all things in the heaven and in the earth. I heard many things in hell. How, then, am I mad? Hearken! and observe how healthily — how calmly I can tell you the whole story.

It is impossible to say how first the idea entered my brain; but once conceived, it haunted me day and night. Object there was none. Passion there was none. I loved the old man. He had never wronged me. He had never given me insult. For his gold I had no desire. I think it was his eye! yes, it was this! He had the eye of a vulture — a pale blue eye, with a film over it. Whenever it fell upon me, my blood ran cold; and so by degrees — very gradually — I made up my mind to take the life of the old man, and thus rid myself of the eye forever.

Now this is the point. You fancy me mad. Madmen know nothing. But you should have seen me. You should have seen how wisely I proceeded — with what caution — with what foresight — with what dissimulation I went to work! I was never kinder to the old man than during the whole week before I killed him. And every night, about midnight, I turned the latch of his door and opened it — oh so gently! And then, when I had made an opening sufficient for my head, I would put in a dark lantern, all closed, closed, so that no light shone out, and then I thrust in my head. Oh, you would have laughed to see how cunningly I thrust it in! I moved it slowly — very, very slowly, so that I might not disturb the old man's sleep. It took me an hour to place my whole head within the opening so far that I could see him as he lay upon his bed. Ha! — would a madman have been so wise as this?", "translation": "没错！——我紧张极了——极度、极度可怕的紧张，过去如此，现在也如此；可你为什么偏要说我疯了？这病使我的感官变得敏锐——没有摧毁——也没有迟钝它们。尤其是听觉格外灵敏。我能听到天堂和地狱中的一切。那么，我怎么会疯呢？听着！看我多么健康、多么平静地告诉你整个故事。

无法说出这念头最初是如何进入我的脑海的；但一旦形成，便日夜萦绕着我。没有动机。没有激情。我爱那个老人。他从未亏待过我。他从未侮辱过我。我对他的金子毫无欲望。我想是他的眼睛！是的，就是它！他有一只秃鹫般的眼睛——一只淡蓝色的眼睛，上面蒙着一层薄膜。每当它落在我身上，我的血液就变冷；于是渐渐地——非常缓慢地——我下定决心要杀死这个老人，从而永远摆脱那只眼睛。

现在关键是这点。你以为我疯了。疯子什么都不知道。但你该看看我。你该看看我多么聪明地行动——多么谨慎——多么有远见——多么虚伪地动手！在杀死他的前一周里，我从未待他如此亲切。而每到半夜，我转动他房门的插销，打开门——哦，如此轻柔！然后，当我开够能伸进头的缝隙时，我便放进一盏暗灯笼，所有缝隙都关紧，不让一丝光透出，然后我探进头去。哦，你该笑看我多么狡猾地探进头！我移动得很慢——很慢很慢，以免打扰老人的睡眠。我花了一个小时才把头完全伸进去，直到能看见他躺在床上的样子。哈！——疯子能像我这样聪明吗？", "key_sentence_patterns": [{"pattern": "It was... that...", "explanation": "强调结构：正是……（使得……）。例如：It was his eye that made me want to kill him."}, {"pattern": "How + adj/adv + subject + verb!", "explanation": "感叹句结构：多么……啊！例如：How calmly I can tell you the story!"}, {"pattern": "I had been + adj; but am", "explanation": "过去完成时与现在时的对比，表示持续状态。例如：nervous I had been and am."}, {"pattern": "so that + clause", "explanation": "目的状语从句：以便……。例如：so that I might not disturb the old man's sleep."}, {"pattern": "would have + past participle", "explanation": "虚拟语气：本会……。例如：you would have laughed to see how cunningly I thrust it in."}], "key_grammar": [{"point": "过去完成进行时", "example": "I had been nervous; the disease had sharpened my senses."}, {"point": "强调结构 It was...that", "example": "It was his eye that made me decide to kill him."}, {"point": "复杂定语从句", "example": "He had the eye of a vulture — a pale blue eye, with a film over it. Whenever it fell upon me, my blood ran cold."}, {"point": "并列结构", "example": "with what caution — with what foresight — with what dissimulation I went to work!"}, {"point": "虚拟语气（与过去事实相反）", "example": "Would a madman have been so wise as this?"}], "vocabulary_focus": ["nervous", "dreadfully", "sharpened", "acute", "conceived", "haunted", "vulture", "film", "dissimulation", "cunningly", "latch", "lantern"], "common_mistakes": "学习者常混淆过去完成进行时和现在完成进行时；误用强调结构中的 that 为 what；忽略虚拟语气中 would have done 的用法。", "tags": ["horror", "guilt", "Edgar Allan Poe", "classic", "psychological"], "author": "Edgar Allan Poe"}
